output.answer: Rivian does not have a parent company. As of today, Rivian Automotive, Inc. is an independent, publicly traded American automaker — a Delaware corporation whose Class A common stock trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RIVN, and it files its own financial statements with the SEC (most recently its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026). Volkswagen (its largest shareholder at roughly 15.9% as of May 2026) and Amazon (about 10.9% of voting power as of July 10, 2026) are major shareholders, not parent companies — Rivian remains independently run with founder RJ Scaringe as CEO.
caveats: Exact current shareholding percentages fluctuate: Amazon's 10.9% voting-power figure is from Rivian's 10-Q as of July 10, 2026, and Volkswagen's ~15.9% figure is a secondary-source estimate as of May 2026, so stakes may have changed since.

While no shareholder is a parent, large holders like Volkswagen and Amazon have significant influence through investments, a joint venture (Rivian and VW Group Technologies, LLC), and commercial relationships.

output.question: Who is the parent company of Rivian?

key_facts.fact: Rivian Automotive, Inc., together with its consolidated subsidiaries, is an independent Delaware corporation (incorporated March 26, 2015) that files its own quarterly financial statements with the SEC — it has no corporate parent.
Rivian's Class A common stock is registered and publicly traded on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol RIVN.

Amazon (via Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC, itself a subsidiary of Amazon) beneficially owns Rivian shares representing 10.9% of Rivian's voting power as of July 10, 2026 — a large shareholder, not a parent.
Volkswagen is Rivian's largest shareholder at roughly 15.9% as of May 2026, but does not own or control Rivian; the company remains independently run with its own board and CEO (founder RJ Scaringe).
Rivian's legal-entity record reports no parent company — it is independently owned rather than a subsidiary, with no foreign or domestic parent.

Primary-source confirmation: Volkswagen-US Holding, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Volkswagen AG, beneficially owns Rivian shares representing 14.1% of voting power as of July 10, 2026 — a large minority stake, not a controlling/parent interest (supersedes the earlier ~15.9% secondary-source estimate from May 2026).
